## The export format

A NanoDrop One UV-Vis export holds one block per measurement: the sample
name, a timestamp, a `Wavelength (nm)` header, some `//` calibration lines, and
then wavelength/absorbance pairs:

```
6 1
5/14/2024 5:04 PM
Wavelength (nm)	10mm Absorbance
//WLCalib: Shift 	0.22333
...
//QSpecEnd:
190.0	10.666
190.5	10.782
...
```

`read_nanodrop()` turns this into a long table with one row per measurement and
wavelength.

## Reading one file

```{r read}
library(nanodRop)

path <- system.file("extdata", "nanodrop_example.tsv", package = "nanodRop")
spectra <- read_nanodrop(path)
head(spectra)
```

The columns are:

- `samps`: sample name as typed on the instrument
- `waves`: wavelength (nm)
- `abs`: absorbance
- `measurement`: position of the block in the file. If you measure the same
  sample twice, the two measurements stay separate.
- `timestamp`: timestamp line as written by the instrument

Use `min_wv` and `max_wv` to keep part of the spectrum:

```{r range}
visible <- read_nanodrop(path, min_wv = 400, max_wv = 700)
range(visible$waves)
```

### Re-measured samples

Some labs mark a re-measurement by adding a suffix to the sample name, for
example `"A"` followed later by `"Ae"`. Set `remeasure_suffix` to have the
re-measurement replace the original:

```{r remeasure, eval = FALSE}
read_nanodrop(path, remeasure_suffix = "e")
```

Only names whose original is also in the file are affected. A sample called
`"Rinse"` stays `"Rinse"` unless there is also a sample called `"Rins"`.

## Reading a folder of exports

`read_nanodrop_dir()` reads every `.tsv` file in a folder and adds a `file`
column:

```{r dir}
folder <- system.file("extdata", package = "nanodRop")
all_spectra <- read_nanodrop_dir(folder)
unique(all_spectra$file)
```

## Plotting

```{r plot, fig.alt = "Absorbance spectra of all samples in the example file, wavelength on the x-axis and absorbance on the y-axis, one coloured line per measurement."}
library(ggplot2)

ggplot(spectra, aes(waves, abs, colour = samps, group = measurement)) +
  geom_line() +
  labs(x = "Wavelength (nm)", y = "Absorbance", colour = "Sample") +
  theme_minimal()
```
